Date: 2026-10-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: Subprocessor custody details & KMS residency for SOC 2

Hi Avery,

We're starting our SOC 2 readiness assessment and the auditor asked us to provide a concise subprocessor custody map specific to data used in inference (model keys, ephemeral tokenization, KV caches). They also want KMS residency and key-hierarchy details for any provider that holds or can retrieve plaintext tokens or model artifacts.

Can you provide:
- A roster of current subprocessors (name, country of operation, type of access — e.g., plaintext, encrypted-with-KMS, no-access) for inference runtime and telemetry
- KMS residency matrix (where keys reside; control plane vs customer-managed) and whether HSM/KMS attestation exists
- Any planned changes in the next 90 days (onboarding/offboarding)

Target deadline from our side is Nov 10 to allow time to compile for auditors. Please let me know if Nov 3 would work for a first-pass evidence packet.

Thanks,

-- 
Elena Ruiz
Senior Procurement Manager
HelixMed
elena.ruiz@helixmed.com

Subject: Re: Request: Subprocessor custody details & KMS residency for SOC 2

Hi Elena — thanks for the note and the timeline.

We can deliver a first-pass packet by Nov 3. Attaching the roster (subprocessor_roster_v2.csv) and a KMS residency matrix (kms-residency-matrix.pdf) to this message for immediate review. Those attachments are a compact summary; we will follow up with an evidence bundle (signed attestations, CAIQ sections, and audit excerpts) by Nov 3.

Quick summary of what you'll find in the attachments:
- subprocessor_roster_v2.csv — lists each subprocessor, primary function (inference runtime, telemetry, storage), country, and access level (plaintext/KMS/no access)
- kms-residency-matrix.pdf — shows key ownership (redwood-managed vs customer-managed KMS), region of residency, and whether HSM-backed keys are used

Next steps we propose:
1) We (Marissa and Karthik) will assemble an evidence TOC and drop a shared Drive folder by Nov 1.
2) Marissa will coordinate signed attestations and export-control/residency statements for onshore subprocessors.
3) Karthik will confirm ephemeral key flows and provide a one-page diagram showing how KV cache and prefixes are protected.

Marissa / Karthik — can you confirm you can hit these dates? Also logging this activity in SIG-912 (linked below).

Best,
